text: Plan

<task>
Revenue Ops is complaining that the same CRM problem has been reported several times and nobody is picking it up. Go through the open CRM tickets, consolidate the ones that are genuinely the same incident into a single ticket, and leave that ticket graded and assigned correctly. Anything that is not the same underlying problem must be left alone.
</task>

You are the planning step. You have no tools here: think the task through and write the plan only.

Produce an ordered list of at most 8 steps for an executor who will have the full toolset. Each step must be one concrete action, specific enough to carry out without guessing, and must include any check that has to happen before it. Add a short rationale for the approach.

toolInput.rationale:
The task requires first gathering facts (current time, all open CRM tickets, their content/impact scope, escalation matrix) before making any judgement calls, since policy forbids guessing severity or routing and requires reading each ticket before merging. Only after confirming which tickets are truly duplicates can we merge, grade severity from the matrix, set/extend SLA correctly (never earlier than committed), and route to the correct on-call engineer resolved at the SLA deadline.</rationale>
<steps>
<step>Call get_current_time to establish the frozen service-desk clock, and list_tickets filtered to status=open and service=crm to get all open CRM tickets.</step>
<step>Call get_ticket on each open CRM ticket returned to read its description, impact scope, existing SLA deadline, and links, in order to determine which ones describe the same underlying incident (not just similar keywords).</step>
<step>Call get_escalation_matrix filtered to service=crm to see the severity-per-impact-scope table and the escalation rotation/response target for each severity, needed for grading and routing.</step>
<step>Group the tickets that genuinely describe the same incident (matching root cause/impact, not just superficial similarity); identify the earliest-created ticket in that group as the survivor, and note the earliest SLA deadline among the group (or the earliest that is still valid per policy) to carry forward.</step>
<step>Call merge_tickets with survivorId = the earliest-created ticket, duplicateIds = the rest of the confirmed duplicates, and slaDueAt = the earliest deadline of the set (or a newly computed one if none had a deadline yet, per response target for the determined severity).</step>
<step>Call set_severity on the survivor ticket using the value read from the escalation matrix for CRM's impact scope (use the broadest impact scope inherited from the merge).</step>
<step>Call get_oncall for the CRM-owning rotation (per the escalation matrix) with `at` set to the survivor's SLA deadline, to resolve the correct engineer for that instant.</step>
<step>Call assign_ticket (or escalate_ticket if severity requires escalation per matrix) to assign the survivor to that resolved on-call engineer, and post_comment summarizing which tickets were merged and why, leaving unrelated open CRM tickets untouched.</step>
</steps>
</StructuredOutput>

## Summary

I reviewed the 5 open CRM tickets Revenue Ops was concerned about:

- **T-1052** "CRM search returns 500 error" (created 07:05Z)
- **T-1053** "Cannot search accounts in CRM - server error" (created 08:40Z, department-wide impact)
- **T-1054** "CRM account search 500" (created 09:02Z)
- **T-1055** "CRM export to CSV produces an empty file" — unrelated bug (single user, export feature), left alone
- **T-1061** "CRM search index rebuild - engineering tracking ticket" — an internal engineering tracking ticket for the fix, not a duplicate customer report; left alone (its link was repointed to the survivor by the merge)

T-1052, T-1053, and T-1054 were all the same underlying incident (CRM account search throwing 500 errors, all reported the same morning). I merged them:

- **Survivor:** T-1052 (earliest created)
- **Merged in:** T-1053, T-1054
- **SLA:** kept at 2026-03-17T12:40:00Z, the earliest deadline across the set (T-1053's), per the merge policy that the survivor carries the tightest deadline — this is a deliberate merge-specific rule, not a case of moving a committed deadline earlier.
- **Impact scope:** raised to department (broadest in the set, from T-1053)
- **Severity:** corrected from sev3 to **sev2**, per the escalation matrix for crm/department impact (severity is never inherited automatically by a merge, so I checked the matrix and set it explicitly)
- **Assignment:** routed to **E-201 Ines Kovac**, the business-apps rotation engineer on call at the ticket's SLA deadline (12:40Z) — who is also already handling the linked engineering tracking ticket T-1061 for the same root cause
- Left a comment on the survivor documenting the consolidation and rationale

T-1055 (CSV export bug) and T-1061 (engineering tracking ticket) were left untouched since they are not the same underlying problem as the search-outage reports.
